parameters.title: Model parameters
parameters.description: Adjust risk, exposure, portfolio and data-quality parameters for this portfolio. Changes are applied to existing scores after leaving a field and saved automatically.

catalog.title: Providers

hailEal.what: Expected annual loss (EAL) from hail for the locations shown.
hailEal.how: EAL = N × λ × (pₛ·Sₛ + pₘ·Sₘ + pₗ·Sₗ). N = vehicles counted on the lot (estimated from the area without a detection model), λ = hail events per year by hail zone, p = share of small/medium/large events, S = loss per vehicle. Values under “Parameters → Hail EAL”.
hailEal.limits: λ, p, and S are uncalibrated placeholders; vehicle counts marked ≈ are area-based estimates. A screening estimate, not a tariff, underwriting, or insurance decision.

accumulations.what: Groups of locations that a single hail event could hit together – sorted by exposure.
accumulations.how: Two locations belong together when they are at most {{radius}} km apart; neighbors form chains (single linkage). Loss scenario = accumulation exposure × {{scenario}} damage ratio.
accumulations.limits: The radius is an assumption about the typical size of a hail cell; storm tracks and weather situations are not modeled. The loss scenario is not a PML from a catastrophe model.

zones.what: How locations or exposure spread across hail zones 1 (low) to 6 (very high).
zones.how: Zone from the postcode hail-zone table; without a postcode it is estimated from the weather-based hail score (shown in the tooltip).
zones.limits: Hail zones describe regional hazard, not the condition of the individual site.

topLocations.what: The locations with the highest expected hail loss per year.
topLocations.how: Sorted by hail EAL (€). The badge shows the hail zone; “≈” = estimated zone.
topLocations.limits: The EAL depends strongly on the vehicle count – manually reviewed counts improve the ranking.

review.what: Locations an underwriter should look at more closely, with the rule that raised the note.
review.how: Critical: hail zone ≥ {{zone}}; share of the portfolio EAL ≥ {{share}}; accumulation within {{radius}} km with exposure ≥ {{threshold}}. Data quality: utilisation > {{utilisation}}, boundary confidence ≤ {{confidence}}, 0 detected vehicles, estimated hail zone. Thresholds under “Parameters”.
review.limits: Rule-based and unweighted – a note is a request to review, not a decline.

about.title: Where the figures come from
about.what: Observations of the nearest German Weather Service stations within {{radius}} km that have at least ten years of records.
about.hailDay: A hail day is a day on which hail was observed at the station – regardless of stone size or damage. A year counts when at least 180 days were validly observed.
about.limits: Point observations, not an event catalogue: hail that misses the station is missing. Many stations stopped observing around 2011.
about.eal: Context only – the figures do not enter the hail EAL.
about.source: Data basis: Deutscher Wetterdienst (Climate Data Center, daily weather phenomena).

notes.far: The station is {{distance}} km away – hail at the site can differ considerably.
notes.short_one: Only {{count}} observed year – the mean is uncertain.
notes.short_other: Only {{count}} observed years – the mean is uncertain.
notes.gaps_one: {{count}} year in the period without sufficient observation (grey).
